READING THIS VIEW

Radar edges sit near the foot of the dune. Optical water edges sit near the wet/dry edge. Neither is "the coastline" on its own.

A sensor shift smaller than one pixel (10 m here) is not resolvable.
WHAT EACH SENSOR ACTUALLY SEES

Accuracy against the lidar line each sensor should match.

Error is sensor minus lidar position along the beach, pooled over all dates (+ means the sensor puts the line further seaward). RMSE is the typical size of the miss. Brackets are 95% intervals from resampling 50 m stretches of beach.

CAN WE TRUST THIS?

Every claim, with its evidence level.

Tags are assigned by fixed rules from the numbers, not by hand. The rules are listed below the claims.

INDEPENDENT TEST

Do the satellites beat a simple guess?

Here each test holds out a whole date and a 100 m stretch of beach; everything tuned or calibrated is learned only from other dates and places, and no evaluation lidar is used inside any method. Every method in a group is scored on the same rows. "Typical position" just predicts where that lidar line usually is.

HOW CLAIMS ARE TAGGED
    OBSERVATION TIMELINE

    When each image was taken, and how high the water was.

    Times are UTC. Water level is from NOAA gauge 8651370 at Duck (m, NAVD88), interpolated to the image time. A different water level moves the visible waterline, which is why timing matters.

    The September nor'easter is not part of this package: wave records were not ingested, so the app makes no storm claim.

    SOURCES & LIMITS

    Evidence before interpretation.

    Full citations with URLs and access dates are in CITATIONS.md in the repository. Everything in this app is generated from the repository's pipeline by src/export_app_data.py.

      DATA USED

      Products

      PROJECT

      An independent NASA Space Apps project.

      Not an official NASA, ISRO or USACE product. Beach lowering is measured by lidar; satellites are compared with it, and no satellite here is shown to measure the lowering on its own. Fusion of sensors is future work. AI assistants (Claude, Gemini) helped write the code and text; the team reviewed the results.

      HOW TO READ THIS APP

      Which coastline does each satellite see?

      The coloured map is real tower-lidar elevation change between June 19 and October 16, 2026. The lines on it are where each satellite puts a boundary on every 10 m row of beach.

      Click the map to open that row's cross-section: the June and October beach profiles, the area that lowered, and every sensor's edge.

      Sensors & trust lists each sensor's accuracy and every claim with its evidence level.

      Radar and optical satellites mark different features. Lines that disagree are not necessarily wrong.
